results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 52 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph (p01-p53) in spec order; the five opening callouts match no paragraph, as expected.

results.quote: Vinted met the same capacity pressure at larger scale inside one cross-border catalog: its 2023 series on moving from MySQL to Vitess describes an autumn peak that strained MySQL
results.finding: The outliner read two ideas: Tradeyard's shared-cluster cost and plan, and Vinted's MySQL-to-Vitess history. The spec's unifying idea (the same capacity pressure, met two ways) is buried under the Vitess numbers (42 servers, 23 shards, 3 TB), so the second half reads as a separate topic. Both flow readers lost the point here.

results.quote: The table also shows the cost of not having the registry: the first answer took two days of investigation
results.finding: The outliner read two ideas: the response sent in nine days, and the registry removing investigation for future requests. The paragraph joins them through a false claim about the table instead of one controlling idea (the first case cost nine days and two of search; at 1,900 a month the next must cost none).

Every unit traces to the thesis: intro and scene pose the question; concepts and architecture support S1-S3; partitioning S1; retention S4; erasure S5; corrections S2; in-practice, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, CA view and questions apply the supporting claims; the conclusion synthesizes them.

results.quote: The table also shows the cost of not having the registry: the first answer took two days of investigation
results.finding: The sentence attributes to Femke's outcome table something it does not contain: the two days of investigation come from the scene, not the table. Both flow readers looked back at the table for it (A item 6, B item 11).

The other evidence is explained: the seven-copy table (four observations), kinds-of-copy table (the rule), store-type table and Figure 2, registry entry, partitioning table, retention schedule (two judgement rows), Figures 1-5 by captions and surrounding prose, Femke's outcomes, trade-off and vertical tables (lead-ins and the contested row / real-estate case), and the Fowler and Vinted quotations, each with the point it supports.

results.quote: That makes Vinted the counter-case to country partitioning: its members widely buy across borders
results.finding: Declared contrast from Vinted's scaling inside one cross-border catalog to Vinted as counter-case. At the boundary the preceding sentence ends on Vitess shard counts, which do not make Vinted a counter-case; 'That makes' points back at the numbers and the reason (cross-border buying) arrives only after it. Both flow readers reported this boundary (A item 4, B item 5).

All other transition_in entries (p02-p53) are expressed at their boundaries with the declared relationship, e.g. 'The copies need names.', 'The concepts now need stores.', 'With the stores in place', 'Those obligations differ by data class', 'An erasure request tests both the registry and the retention schedule', 'Preventing these failures takes few decisions'.

The does_not_know terms are given in the draft: system of record and the seven kinds of copy (Concepts), staleness budget and the four promises (Concepts), erasure case and ledger (workflow steps 1 and 6), crypto-shredding (backups list), GDPR/DSA/Dutch rules (Retention, Erasure). Other terms the flow readers listed (Veldmark brands, Yardstick, Safe Deal, version gate, backfill topic, state topic, ListingErased) are on already_knows; p95/p99, CDC, surrogate key and strangler are baseline vocabulary for this audience.
The introduction opens from the previous chapter's consequence (copies) and three concrete questions, with stakes and scope; no dictionary opener, throat-clearing or announcement-only pattern.
The conclusion is not a restatement-only summary or a new topic: it answers the three questions, gives the so-what and a takeaway, and hands off.

'The three questions ... have one answer: a list of copies kept before anyone needs it' synthesizes; 'the next of about 1,900 monthly requests needs no investigation' answers so-what; takeaway 'Register every copy before the next store gets access.'
Calls back to the opening's three questions and Femke's seven copies found in two days because no list existed.

The intro reader predicted the scene (one bike in seven places), concepts, architecture, partitioning, retention, erasure, corrections, Vinted/Adevinta practice, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, CA view and questions in roadmap order, with GDPR, DSA, Dutch rules, Vinted/Adevinta and fictional Veldmark as evidence; matches the roadmap and expected.

The reader handles the request as an erasure case resolved to identifiers with a fan-out event and a receipt per copy into the erasure ledger, gives each copy's outcome as expected (SoR anonymized, sold page 410 + CDN purge + removal request, media deleted, warehouse personal-data rows deleted, fraud case retained under legal claims to a stated end, payment records retained 7 years with restricted access, e-mail provider instructed), says registration makes the next case need no search, and fixes the complaint by serving seller pages from the SoR (read-your-writes) with per-read-path promises for other readers.

The reader names replica, search index and cache as rebuildable (freshness, owner, budget, purge) and archive, evidence store, warehouse (only partly) and e-mail logs as not, with the governance expected for each (purpose and retention, legal basis and access control, personal-data split and erasure job, contract and Art. 19 notification and delete path), under the rule 'rebuildable or governed'.

The reader chooses country-first partitioning (schema per country, country in every key, hashing within a large country), a single writer per brand with nearby read models, replicas inheriting retention and erasure, and says global hashing fits one huge market or a cross-border catalog like Vinted and multi-writer only when latency or sovereignty demands it, citing Vinted's 2026 reasoning; matches expected.
